account: It is day one, six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. I have not yet seen today's activity. I should go to my office and read the appointment books. The original schedule lists office at eight, a mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen. Yesterday I also confirmed a brief great hall lighting inspection with the builder today at eighteen. The builder says eight lanterns are installed and nothing needs reviewing beforehand. This appears to be ordinary town maintenance. The secretary needed a replacement writable book because the original appointment book was signed; I gave them an emerald and asked them to preserve the original and record the inspection. I have not yet verified that this was done. The only unusual news was vague talk of possible bridge or port changes. The neighbour had no details, the secretary knew of no verified proposal, and the builder said they had no such works proposed. I cannot conclude there is any actual project. I also heard reports yesterday of the baker carrying a sack of bread, and saw freight give the baker an emerald. Those observations are consistent with ordinary bread business, not evidence of anything improper. I heard an indistinct distant shout from freight but could not understand it, so I do not know its purpose.
